card.name: Word 'combined' or 'concomitant' in drug interactions
card.fires_on: Words meaning use together, such as concomitant (including its inner pieces), combined, or 'are used' after two named drugs, in drug interaction passages. It also fires on a few drug-name pieces in interaction text.

modes.label: Together-use words
modes.description: Concomitant, combined, or similar words just before 'use' or 'therapy' when two drugs are given together.
modes.example: Cases of life‑threatening serotonin syndrome have been reported during<< combined>> use of SSRIs or SNRIs

modes.label: Inside concomitant
modes.description: The first piece or middle of the word concomitant.
modes.example: The risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis is increased with<< con>>comitant use.

modes.label: Drug name pieces
modes.description: Pieces inside a drug name in interaction advice about a second drug.

card.writes: It favors words about things being mutual or paired, such as 'pairwise', 'interconnected', and 'each other'.
card.plain: It lights up when the text is about two drugs being taken together.
